correctness.rationale: For fixed length, a squarefree CRT modulus and Weyl equidistribution give p-local factor 1-min(p,r)/p^2. Holdridge 2026 Theorem 1.3, read in full theorem statement and final proof, supplies the uniformly vanishing large-prime tail for each of finitely many integer-constant translates of f. Endpoint inclusion-exclusion gives delta=C_r-2C_{r+1}+C_{r+2}. A local two-large-prime construction proves strict positivity. The exact ratio Q_r=prod_{p>r}(1-1/(p^2-r)) and delta/C=(1-Q)^2+Q(Q_next-Q) are algebraic identities. Mertens and PNT give C_r~exp(-gamma)/log r and 1-Q_r~1/(r log r). If r+1 composite, Q_next-Q=O(r^-3); if prime, Q_next-Q~r^-2. This establishes both sharp leading-constant regimes. Actual standard-library checker returned VERIFY_OK finite_checks=166 and is not promoted to an infinite proof. Scientific limitations and sequential limit order appear in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: The natural maximal-run statistic attached to floor-polynomial coprimality admits a complete positive exact density profile. Its new structurally sharp feature is a factor (log r)^2 prime-successor enhancement, with leading constants, against composite-successor lengths, uniformly across a large analytic family. This quantifies a nonobvious prime-sensitive long-run phenomenon beyond the already-known one-point zeta density and the numerically existing Euler product; it is a meaningful infinite classification, not an arbitrary small cutoff, a textbook substitution, or a finite numerical gain.
